# Blazor

- BLZ-001: Component authors should avoid coupling a component's implementation to a specific render mode, and should typically design components to support any render mode or hosting model. In most cases, reusable component authors should not specify a render mode, even when interactivity is required.
- BLZ-003: For two-way data binding, the @bind:get/@bind:set modifiers are recommended. Specifying a culture with @bind:culture isn't recommended when using the date and number field types.
- BLZ-008: Avoid thousands of component instances. For components that render at scale, such as each item in a large list or the cells of a grid, try to avoid attribute splatting. Avoid recreating delegates for many repeated elements or components, and don't trigger events too rapidly. Most Razor components don't require aggressive optimization efforts, because most components don't repeat in the UI and don't rerender at high frequency.
- BLZ-019: In production, don't render framework exception messages or stack traces in the UI. Narrowly scoping error boundaries is recommended in most scenarios.
- BLZ-021: Always use the @formname directive attribute with a unique form name. To mitigate overposting, using a separate view model or data transfer object (DTO) for the form and the database in create (insert) and update operations is recommended.
